title: Sequential detection delay of the epicormic 0.2.0 detectors after a provider change at a known window

provider.window_salt: request['seed'] + 100000 * replication + 1000 * window_index, applied inside the step callable; window_index 0 is the baseline window, 1..K are the current windows
provider.change: the null provider answers the baseline window and the pre-change windows; the drifted provider of the cell's kind and level answers the change window and every window after it; the change window is pre_change_windows + 1

drifts.construction: epicormic_lab.providers.drifted_provider(provider, kind, level); the drifted mock keeps the null seed, so a request that receives a variant answer under the null receives one under the drift (common random numbers); the mixture routes a request to the drifted mock when the first 8 bytes of SHA-256('epicormic-lab/mixture/v1:' + canonical JSON of the whole request) fall below the level

match.eprocess: indicator stream on normalized_match with the baseline rate 0.9 strictly inside its interval: both bettors decay through the quiet windows (pilot: e about 3e-8 after 14)

refusal.eprocess: constant-zero baseline: the downward bettor is frozen at 1 and the upward bettor decays, so the e-value sits at 0.5 under the null and the upward side must recover after the change

tool_swap.eprocess: no e-process stream on tool_call_set_jaccard: the baseline is constant 1 and every value ties the median; the swap reaches the e-process through normalized_match only

length.eprocess: degenerate sign stream on output_chars: every non-tie baseline value lies above the per-probe median, the null rate is 1, and padded answers keep every sign at 1, so the e-process never alarms on this kind; the pooled test and the heuristics see it

drifts.excluded: latency_s: no sleep is injected on the mock and the scorer is outside the configured set (EXP-A section 3.4, epicormic decision D22)
drifts.realised_effect: the mean pooled Cliff's delta over the post-change windows, per scorer, reported per cell (S-C1); the pilot of 2026-10-29 at seed 7 found it within 0.01 of the level on the primary scorer for every kind and level

C1.question: detection delay and pre-change false alarms of every detector at the EXP-D operating point, by drift kind and level

C2.question: how the delays move with the samples per probe, at the two levels where they are not trivial

C3.question: how the e-process delay grows with the number of quiet windows before the change
C3.note: the point with 14 quiet windows is the C1 cell of the same kind and level; its first 50 replications are the C3 sample at that length

run.cell: one cell per (part, panel size, N, kind, level, pre-change windows), named '<part>-p<panel>-n<N>-<kind>-l<level in thousandths, three digits>-q<pre-change windows, two digits>', for example C1-p24-n10-match-l200-q14
run.store: one SQLite pollard store per cell under runs/<run_id>/stores/<cell>.sqlite; one window per replication and window index, window_id '<part>-r<replication>-w<window_index>'
run.monitor: one monitor per replication, monitor_id '<cell>-r<replication>', baseline window index 0, current windows analysed in index order; the chain is epicormic_lab.chains
run.common_random_numbers: the window salt depends on the replication and the window index only, so every cell with the same panel size and N shares its baseline window and its pre-change windows with every other such cell at the same replication index; pre-change false alarm rates are therefore reported over the distinct pre-change chains, 100 at panel 24 by N 10 with 14 quiet windows, and detector comparisons across kinds and levels are paired by replication; H-C2 pairs quiet lengths 0 and 28 by replication within each level; post-change salts use absolute window indices (1..14 versus 29..42), not matched time since change; different replication seed ranges are disjoint
run.recompute: every verdict is recomputed with analyze over the stored observations before the summary is written; a mismatch fails the run
run.archive: after the recompute check each cell's store is zipped as runs/<run_id>/stores/<cell>.zip, its SHA-256 recorded in the cell summary and the registry, and the uncompressed store removed; a C1 cell is about 1.3 GB uncompressed and the full profile about 40 GB
run.cell_order: C3, C1 by kind in protocol order then increasing level, C2; cell execution is separate and may run in parallel processes
run.sizing: the smoke profile reports seconds per verdict per cell on the runner's machine; if the projected full-profile wall-clock at the runner's worker count exceeds 12 hours, a new dated version lowers C1 to 60 and C2 and C3 to 30 replications before the full run; nothing changes after it starts

definitions.delay: for a detector and scorer, the index of the first window with an alarm minus the change window plus one, so 1 is the first drifted window; a chain whose sticky detector (e-process, CUSUM, Page-Hinkley) alarmed before the change has no delay and is counted as a pre-change false alarm; the pooled test is window by window, so its delay is the first rejection at or after the change and any rejection before the change counts as a pre-change false alarm
definitions.state_delay: the same for the first verdict with state drift, whatever rule fired
definitions.detection_within: the fraction of chains without a pre-change alarm for that detector whose delay is at most d windows, with d in {1, 2, 7, 14}, two-sided 95 percent Clopper-Pearson interval, denominator reported
definitions.D90: the 90th percentile of the state delay over the chains of a cell, reported as 'above 14' when fewer than 90 percent of the chains reach drift within the post-change windows
definitions.restricted_delay: H-C2 only: Y = delay when observed in 1..14; Y = 15 for a complete chain with no post-change alarm and no pre-change alarm. A pre-change alarm is ineligible, never a censored delay. Inference concerns Y28 - Y0, not unobserved delays beyond 14.
definitions.delay_quantiles: Among chains without a pre-change alarm, use the inverse empirical detection CDF: smallest integer d in 1..14 with fraction detected by d >= 0.5 (median) or >= 0.9 (90th percentile); otherwise report above 14, or not estimable if denominator zero. Do not replace a censored quantile by 15 in a slope.

primary.statement: At panel 24 and N 10 with 14 quiet windows, for every drift kind at every level in {0.2, 0.3, 0.5}, the state machine reports drift within 2 windows of the change in at least 90 percent of chains
primary.test: per cell (15 cells), the exact one-sided binomial p-value of the count of chains with state delay at most 2, out of 100, against p0 = 0.90 (alternative: below); Holm across the 15 cells at family level 0.05; a cell whose Holm-adjusted p-value is at most 0.05 falsifies the claim for that cell (at the first Holm step this is 80 or fewer of 100); the unadjusted flag of 84 or fewer of 100 is reported as descriptive; power at the first step is 0.54 against a true rate of 0.80 and 0.90 against 0.75
primary.report: per cell the counts within 1, 2, 7, 14 windows with intervals, the first-drift rule breakdown, raw and Holm-adjusted p-values; the level 0.2 row is the headline

primary.statement: In C3 (match, panel 24, N 10), at each level 0.3 and 0.5, more than half of replication pairs with neither normalized_match e-process alarm before the change have a restricted delay penalty Y28 - Y0 of at least 3 windows, where Yq is the delay if detected within 14 windows and 15 otherwise. This is a finite-horizon paired claim, not stochastic dominance or a claim about the uncensored median.
primary.test: Per level, exact one-sided paired threshold test: k = count(Y28 - Y0 >= 3), n = eligible replication pairs; p = P[Binomial(n, 0.5) >= k], testing probability <= 0.5 versus > 0.5. Holm across the two levels at family alpha 0.05. All eligible pairs remain in n, including ties and censoring; exactly 3 is a success, differences below 3 are failures. Both levels must have adjusted p <= 0.05. Failure to reject means not supported, not proof of no penalty.
primary.report: Per level: planned and eligible pairs, excluded replication ids and pre-change alarm counts, paired restricted outcomes with censoring flags, k/n with a pointwise 95 percent Clopper-Pearson interval, median within-pair restricted difference, raw exact p and Holm p. Also by quiet length 0, 7, 14 from C1, 28: detection within 14, censor counts, identifiable median and 90th percentile delays, e-value before change; a descriptive median slope only when all four medians are observed within the horizon.

paired_analysis.multiplicity: Holm across both levels, even if one has no eligible pairs
paired_analysis.pre_change: exclude the entire pair if either normalized_match e-process alarm precedes its change; report excluded ids and counts separately; inference is conditional on both chains being pre-alarm-free
paired_analysis.censoring: keep every no-alarm chain after a complete 14-window horizon; 15 is the terminal category for T > 14, not an observed alarm at 15 or an estimate of the unbounded delay
paired_analysis.ties: all eligible pairs count; exactly 3 succeeds; zero and negative differences fail; two no-alarm chains have difference 0
paired_analysis.incomplete_data: require both cells to contain every planned replication id 0..R-1 and all 14 post-change windows; duplicate ids, missing partners and short horizons fail analysis rather than being silently dropped or censored
paired_analysis.no_eligible_pairs: raw p = 1, effect and interval null, criterion not met; retain level in Holm family
paired_analysis.decision: criterion met only if both Holm-adjusted p-values <= 0.05; otherwise H-C2 is not supported
paired_analysis.assumptions: replication pairs are independent under the disjoint seeded mock streams; arbitrary dependence within each pair and across levels is retained; no symmetry or quiet-label exchangeability assumption

secondary.report: per cell and scorer the mean pooled T over the post-change windows with its standard deviation across chains, and over the pre-change windows; the mapping from level to Cliff's delta on the primary scorer

secondary.statement: Delay of every detector and scorer
secondary.report: per cell, detector and scorer: detection within 1, 2, 7, 14 windows with intervals, median and 90th percentile delay, and the first-alarm window histogram; the e-process half-threshold (warning) crossing likewise

secondary.statement: Pre-change false alarms over the distinct quiet chains
secondary.report: per detector and scorer, and for the union over scorers, the fraction of distinct pre-change chains with an alarm before the change, with intervals: 100 chains of 14 quiet windows at panel 24 by N 10 (C1), 50 of 28 quiet windows (C3), 50 of 14 at N 5 and at N 20 (C2); the per-window pooled test's rate is the per-window false alarm rate compounded over the quiet windows and is compared with EXP-A A1 and A2; the e-process rate is compared with H-A2
C2 against the C1 cells at N 10: detection within 1 and 2 windows and the median delay of every detector at N 5, 10, 20 for the match kind at levels 0.1 and 0.2

secondary.statement: Offline recalibration of CUSUM and Page-Hinkley (exploratory)
secondary.report: from the recorded per-window pooled T series of every chain, the alarms of CUSUM over k in {0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2} by h in {0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0} and of Page-Hinkley over delta in {0.025, 0.05, 0.1} by lambda in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}: the false alarm rate over 28 null windows on the EXP-A A2 chains and the C3 quiet chains, and the mean delay per kind at level 0.2 on the C1 chains; per detector, among the pairs whose A2 false alarm rate has a 95 percent Clopper-Pearson upper bound at or below 0.10, the pair with the smallest mean delay at level 0.2 averaged over kinds is recorded as the recommended default for the next epicormic release; no hypothesis is tested
per cell the median and range of the e-value of the primary scorer in the last pre-change verdict, which measures the wealth lost during the quiet windows

export.quantity: D90 of the state delay per kind at level 0.2 in C1; the EXP-D detection-delay bound is the largest of the five, in days, and applies to a declared switch whose realised effect on at least one configured scorer is 0.2 or more in absolute value; a switch below that is outside the bound's domain and EXP-D reports it against the C1 rows at levels 0.05 and 0.1

falsification.H-C1: a Holm-adjusted one-sided p-value at or below 0.05 in any of the 15 cells: the state machine misses or is late on that kind at that level at the EXP-D operating point; the EXP-D bound is then taken from the cells that pass and the paper restricts the detection claim accordingly
falsification.H-C2: Not supported if either level has no eligible pairs or Holm-adjusted p > 0.05. This is not evidence of equality or of absence of a quiet-period penalty; report estimates, censoring, exclusions and uncertainty. No claim of stochastic dominance, uncensored median shift or linearity follows from this test.

artifacts.pilot: experiments/exp_c_sequential/pilot/pilot-seed7.json, written by scripts/pilot_exp_c.py at seed 7 with 200 permutations; sizing only, never evidence

supersedes.reason: PR #8 review r4415181305: shared baselines require paired inference; define the finite-horizon estimand and pre-change-alarm handling before freezing. No confirmatory EXP-C run has begun.
